## In one sentence

Calculus describes change with derivatives and accumulation with integrals.

## Derivatives

The derivative is an instantaneous rate of change:

$$
f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}
$$

A derivative can be interpreted as a slope, sensitivity, or marginal effect.
The chain rule handles nested functions and is central to optimisation and
neural-network training.

## Integrals

An integral accumulates small contributions. The fundamental theorem connects
change and accumulation: integrating a derivative recovers the net change,
subject to the starting value.

## Multivariable calculus

For $f(x_1,\ldots,x_p)$, the gradient collects partial derivatives:

$$
\nabla f = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1}, \ldots, \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_p}\right)
$$

The gradient points toward steepest increase. Directional derivatives describe
change along a chosen direction.

## Check your understanding

For a simple quadratic function, find the derivative, locate its stationary
point, and explain what the derivative says on either side.
